rawItems.title: ATM stolen from petrol station in ANOTHER Cambridgeshire ramraid
rawItems.content: An ATM was stolen from a petrol station in the second Cambridgeshire ram raid this week. Police were called to the BP garage on Wisbech Road, Littleport, at 5.06am this morning (Friday November 6) after reports of a ram raid. Officers arrived 12 minutes later to find the cash machine gone and the telehandler used in the raid abandoned nearby. Police searched the area but found no suspects. Yesterday (Thursday November 5), the force were called at around 3am with reports of an attempted ram raid at the Nationwide building on Ramsey Road in Whittlesey. Police have not confirmed if the two incidents are related. Detective Chief Inspector Chris O’Brien said: "Ram-raids are likely to take place between September and January when the nights are darker. A search of the area was carried out but no suspects were found (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) "Our patrols have increased across the county. "We are committed to making it harder for ATM thieves to target our local shops and ATM machines and will be targeting areas we believe are at increased risk – but we can’t do it alone. "We need the public’s help to report anything suspicious or anything they see that might not seem quite right, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem. "One call could make all the difference and potentially stop a store or petrol station being targeted." rawItems.title: Hunts man due in court accused of employee theft and fraud offences named
rawItems.content: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court. He is alleged to have spent £935.83 on personal items using a company credit card while on leave between August 21 and September 2, knowing the transactions were unauthorised and intending to make financial gain. He is also accused of stealing an Apple iPhone worth £285, a Lenovo laptop worth £478 and several tools, including a drill set. The items belonged to water treatment supplier Prodose Ltd and were allegedly stolen between September 2 and October 14. Between November 13 and December 8, Mr Stokes is accused of stealing tools valued at £2,109.18 from Riverside Waste Machinery Ltd. A further fraud charge alleges that he used or permitted the use of company credit cards for unauthorised transactions totalling £412.41 between October 6 and December 8. All the offences are alleged to have taken place in Huntingdon.
